description: PAT, Precision Agriculture Tools, is a QGIS plugin for processing and analysing precision agriculture data. It cleans high-density on-the-go sensor data such as yield monitor or EM38 soil sensor readings, interpolates them into raster maps, analyses remotely sensed imagery and clusters several datasets into zones. It was developed by the CSIRO Precision Agriculture Team, led by Christina Ratcliff, with support from Wine Australia through the Australian Government's Rural R&D for Profit programme. It is generic in location. It is free to download from the official QGIS plugin repository, with code and a user manual on GitHub; version 1.1.0 of 24 February 2025 is the latest stable release, and earlier releases date back to 2020. The plugin page does not state a licence. Caveats: it runs only on Windows and needs the pyprecag, fiona and rasterio Python libraries, and its releases are infrequent. For simulation it prepares field-scale yield and soil maps that can be used to set up farm water, input and yield models and to map how crop output varies within fields exposed to drought or heat. It is related to the QGIS record in this catalogue, the GIS environment it extends.
